reasons: No tests or error handling are visible in this file.
Quick task form hardcodes the Career category and the medium priority.
Calendar is a placeholder: always 31 days, no weekday alignment.
Hardcoded XP and toast amounts may not match real store awards.
Delete actions have no confirmation step.

terms.meaning: a reusable piece of the screen that combines layout, behavior and data into one named part of the app
the inputs a component receives from the parent that uses it
values a component remembers while it is on screen, such as the open dialog or typed text
the shared place where the app keeps its data, such as tasks and habits, so many screens can read and change it
experience points, a score the app gives for actions to show progress
a short message that appears briefly to confirm an action
the standard world time zone used as the reference clock for dates

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and page setup
sections.what: Brings in the state helper, the shared data stores, the name helper, and every full room view that studio mode can show.
sections.why: Likely reason: the full views are loaded here so studio mode can switch to any room without extra steps.

sections.name: DeskModuleRoomProps
sections.title: Inputs this room receives from its parent
sections.what: Lists the active room name and the callbacks the parent page supplies for navigation, the classic mode switch, the task dialog, and toasts.
sections.why: Likely reason: the parent handles navigation so this room can focus on showing its own content.
sections.watch_out: Renaming or adding a prop means updating every parent that renders this room, or the room will fail to work.

sections.name: ROOM_TITLES
sections.title: Heading text for each room
sections.what: Maps each internal room name to the heading shown in the sheet header, with a generic heading for unknown names.
sections.why: Keeps the visible room names in one place.
sections.watch_out: A room name missing from this list shows the generic Module Room heading instead of its real title.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 1)
sections.title: Loading data and building timer text
sections.what: Reads the signed-in user and pulls tasks, habits, notes, goals, projects, profile and focus timer data from the store, then builds the display name and the focus countdown text with leading zeros.
sections.why: The room shows live data, so it reads it once at the top of the component.
sections.watch_out: The display name falls back to the profile name when the signed-in user has no name.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 2)
sections.title: Dark lights and summary numbers
sections.what: Provides a switch that inverts the whole desk and shows a toast, and calculates task totals, the momentum percentage, today's date and a habit row count.
sections.why: The dark look is a visual switch kept local to this room, and the numbers feed the overview.
sections.watch_out: Today's date is taken in UTC, so near midnight it can differ from the user's local day and habit check-ins may land on the wrong day.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 3)
sections.title: Header and studio view switch
sections.what: Draws the sheet header with the room title, a button that toggles between Cozy Sheet and Full Studio View, and the Home Base button. In studio view it shows the full view for the active room instead of the cozy content.
sections.why: Lets the user pick a rich full page or a simpler tactile page.
sections.watch_out: Studio view replaces the whole body, so the quick-add forms and lists are hidden while it is on.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 4)
sections.title: Quick task add form
sections.what: In the tasks room, shows New Task and Clear Done buttons and a one-line form that adds a task dated today with medium priority, 30 minutes, and the Career category and tag.
sections.why: Likely reason: quick entry without opening a full dialog.
sections.watch_out: Every task added here is labeled Career, whatever the user meant, so tasks may land in the wrong category until edited.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 5)
sections.title: Task list with completion toggle
sections.what: Lists every task with a checkbox. Checking it marks the task done and awards 10 XP with a toast; unchecking returns it to today. Each row shows its due date and category.
sections.why: Basic task tracking with a small reward for finishing.
sections.watch_out: The 10 XP is awarded every time a task is checked, so checking, unchecking and checking again earns XP each time.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 6)
sections.title: Task delete then habit scarf
sections.what: Each task has a delete button that removes it at once with a toast, and an empty message appears when there are no tasks. The habits and systems rooms then start with a knitted scarf strip, one bar per habit streak day, minimum twelve bars, cycling through four colors.
sections.why: Deleting is a quick clean-up action, and the scarf is a visual reward that grows with habit check-ins.
sections.watch_out: A habit with no streak still counts as one bar, so the scarf total is not the same as the number of check-ins.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 7)
sections.title: Habit add form and daily heading
sections.what: Shows the Daily Habits heading, a New Habit button, and a one-line form that creates a daily habit with a 7-day target and Health category, awards 10 XP and shows a toast.
sections.why: Likely reason: quick habit creation, matching the quick task form.
sections.watch_out: XP is awarded right after submitting, without checking that the habit saved.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 8)
sections.title: Habit check-in rows
sections.what: Each habit has a checkbox that logs today's completion when checked, shows a toast promising 60 XP, and shows its streak in days. An empty message appears when there are no habits.
sections.why: Daily check-in is the main habit action.
sections.watch_out: The toast promises 60 XP but this code does not award it, so the real XP depends on store logic not visible here. Also, a checked habit cannot be unchecked here.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 9)
sections.title: Overview numbers and project bars
sections.what: Shows nine summary boxes (tasks done, momentum, XP, streak, habits, focus minutes, level, a balance label, active missions). Each project has a progress bar and a plus 10 percent button that also awards 5 XP.
sections.why: Gives an at-a-glance status of the whole system.
sections.watch_out: The Life Balance box always shows Steady, a fixed label with no calculation behind it.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 10)
sections.title: Overview close and note capture
sections.what: Closes the overview block, then starts the Second Brain part with a text box and Save Note button. Saving stores the note with its first 30 characters as the title and tags it brain.
sections.why: Fast capture of a thought without leaving the desk.
sections.watch_out: The title is saved but never shown here; only the full note text appears in the list.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 11)
sections.title: Saved notes list and delete
sections.what: Lists saved notes by their full text, each with a delete button, and shows an empty message when there are none.
sections.why: Lets the user review and clean up notes.
sections.watch_out: Deleting a note happens at once with no confirmation step.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 12)
sections.title: Awards badges and settings opening
sections.what: Closes the goals list, then shows five awards that unlock from live data and appear greyed out until earned. Then opens the settings area with the signed-in name, level, XP and streak.
sections.why: Awards show progress and encourage use; settings lives inside this room.
sections.watch_out: Awards are recalculated each time and not stored, so an award can flip back to locked if the data it depends on changes.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 13)
sections.title: Classic switch and calendar
sections.what: Settings has a button to switch to the classic sidebar layout. Below it, the calendar shows the current month name and a grid of 31 numbered squares, with today's number highlighted.
sections.why: The classic switch lets the user go back to the older layout. The calendar is a simple visual.
sections.watch_out: The calendar always draws 31 days starting in the Sunday column, so it is wrong for short months and for any month not starting on Sunday.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 14)
sections.title: Focus room timer and mode buttons
sections.what: Shows a large countdown with start or pause, reset, and mode buttons for 50 minute work and 10 minute break. Start always begins a fifty minute sprint named Deep Work Sprint.
sections.why: A simpler timer on the desk, separate from the full focus page.
sections.watch_out: Start and reset use fixed text and a fixed 50 minutes, so the labels will be wrong if the store's mode or length changes.

sections.name: SCARF_COLORS (part 15)
sections.title: Long rest mode and focus totals
sections.what: Adds the 30 minute rest button, shows total focus minutes and the number of focus sessions shown as trees, then closes the layout and renders the shared dialogs.
sections.why: Finishes the focus room and the whole component.
sections.watch_out: All dialogs share one state value, so opening one replaces any other that is open.

summary: The main body of one desk room (tasks, habits, goals, notes and so on), shown either as a hand-drawn cozy sheet or as a full studio view, reading and changing live data through the store.
purpose: Give the user one page per desk room where they can add, check off, delete and review items, and switch to a richer full view when they want.
why: Likely reason: one component handles every room, so the desk only needs to pass in a room name to change what is shown. The reason for having two view styles is not stated in the code, beyond the comments calling them Cozy Sheet and Full Studio View.
how: 1) Reads the signed-in user and the store data (tasks, habits, notes, goals, projects, profile, focus timer). 2) Builds the display name, the focus countdown text, and summary numbers. 3) Keeps local state for the view style, the open dialog, the quick-add text boxes and the dark lights switch. 4) If studio view is on, shows the full view for the active room. 5) Otherwise shows the hand-drawn lists, forms and buttons for that room. 6) Renders the shared dialogs at the bottom.
inputs: The active room name, navigation callbacks, a message callback for toasts, the store data listed above, the signed-in user, and anything the user types or clicks.
outputs: Changes to store data (new or updated tasks, habits, notes, goals, projects, XP, focus timer), short toast messages, navigation requests, and the visual room page.
risks: The quick task form always labels new tasks as Career. The calendar is a fixed grid of 31 days with no real weekday alignment. Several XP amounts and toast texts are hardcoded and may not match what the store really awards. Clear Done and delete buttons act with no confirmation. Today's date is taken in UTC, which can differ from the user's local day late in the evening. The focus room starts a fixed 50 minute sprint.
debug: If a room is blank or shows the generic heading, check the room name passed in against the room title list and the branch conditions. If numbers look wrong, check the calculations near the top and the store fields they read. If a button does nothing, check the store action it calls. The packet labels its sections SCARF_COLORS, but this code is the body of the room component, so rely on the section titles here.
